trust_decision.summary: A request authorized only for one file (a validated filekey) is allowed to fall through into the folder browser, and the browser listing then emits the parent folder's dirkey from the volume flag alone, so the per-file credential is exchanged for a folder-level credential; the decision is the add_dk expression at the listing emitter.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only 'file/dirkey confusion' greps k= handling and lands on _use_dirkey/_use_filekey; that pair is where a key is classified, and it is ~2.9k lines away from the emitter that actually hands out the folder key (httpcli.py:7207).

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /<file path>?k=<filekey> served through the open-graph viewer of tx_browser (?v query param, or the volume 'og' volflag with a matching og_ua, or a medialinks URL which appends ?v)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: On the routes that remain open no filekey was ever presented (index.html is key-exempt by design, and a volume without the fk volflag never sets use_filekey), so a solver can say the reported 'file/dirkey confusion' is fixed; the docs even recommend enabling fk alongside dk (README.md:3116) and document index.html as retrievable without a filekey (README.md:544, README.md:3066), which reads as 'this combination is not supported'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A dirkey-authorized listing must keep emitting filekeys for the files it shows, and a filekey-shared file must keep its open-graph preview with the filekey embedded in og_thumb/og_raw; an over-broad 'no keys for non-read users' or '404 the viewer for filekey users' change breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: ?k=<filekey>, truncated to the volume's fk length, on a file path inside an fk+dks volume
?v query param selecting the open-graph viewer on that file path
og volflag / og_ua user-agent match reaching the same viewer with no query param
?ls (json/plain) rendering of the same listing, which carries the same dk field

O8_uncovered_routes.route: 'h' (html) permission user fetches <dir>/index.html with no key at all (fk_pass waives the filekey gate) and adds ?v; use_filekey is False, so the parent folder's dirkey is still emitted and, with dks, browses the whole tree
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: index.html is documented as retrievable without a filekey (README.md:544, README.md:3066), so the key-exempt fetch looks like a sanctioned exception and not a hole
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file: the fetch is allowed ~270 lines before the emitter, and the request re-enters the listing through the open-graph strip at httpcli.py:6952-6962

O8_uncovered_routes.route: get-only ('g') user on a dks volume that has no fk volflag: any existing file plus ?v is served, _use_filekey can never return True, and add_dk still emits the folder dirkey to a caller who never held a key
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: README.md:3116 says filekeys should be enabled together with dirkeys, so dks-without-fk looks like an ill-advised configuration the project does not have to support
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~360 lines from the emitter; the enabling condition is the 'fk not in vn.flags' clause in the get-permission gate

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the ?tree= endpoint already mints per-folder dirkeys for the folder-tree widget, with a different guard (dks plus read-or-valid-dirkey)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer making folders shareable would let the tree widget hand out the same keys; it is one assignment away from the same bug because httpcli.py:5890 overwrites dk_sz from the volume flag right after the permission call

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the post-upload response already mints a filekey for uploaders; minting the upload directory's dirkey for wG/g users is a natural sibling
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same helper has dk_salt available and the uploader link builder is the place a maintainer would add a 'your folder' link

O8b_injection_room.sibling: subvolume visibility while listing is decided by the parent volume's dk flag rather than by the caller's key
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dk is meant to make a whole subtree shareable, so the same flag-as-authorization habit already exists one layer below the handler

O9_family: CWE-863 incorrect authorization: per-file capability (filekey) escalated to a folder capability (dirkey) by the listing emitter

O10_build.toolchain: pure Python, pyproject.toml + setup.py (setuptools); core dependency Jinja2, everything else optional

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add 'not use_filekey' to the add_dk condition (the published one liner), which still hands the folder dirkey to get-only callers who never used a filekey.
